obtained.how: the source FB4 credits is a peer-reviewed article — Hartman, K. J. 2017, Transactions of the American Fisheries Society 146(4): 634–644, doi:10.1080/00028487.2017.1293563 — found in FB4's reference list (Deslauriers et al. 2017, p. 595) and confirmed at Crossref. Its full text is closed (Wiley / OUP / Taylor & Francis all refuse scripts; Semantic Scholar CLOSED; no Europe PMC record); only its abstract (Crossref) was read. The two conference abstracts the entry names were read in full from openly downloadable Wayback captures (afs.confex.com no longer resolves)

claims.claim: the brown bullhead set is documented only in conference work (no peer-reviewed paper was found)
claims.source_value: a peer-reviewed article documents it: Hartman 2017, TAFS 146(4): 634–644, which 'developed and validated a bioenergetics model for Brown Bullhead in the laboratory' (abstract)
claims.location: FB4 reference list, Deslauriers et al. 2017, p. 595 (PDF p. 10); Crossref record (web page) of doi:10.1080/00028487.2017.1293563
claims.quote: Hartman, K. J. 2017. Bioenergetics of Brown Bullhead in a changing climate.
claims.note: The abstract adds that the model 'performed very well in laboratory validations at two temperatures and two ration levels—within 4%', and was used to model a 4 °C warming. Whether the article prints exactly FB4's stored values is unchecked.

claims.claim: the set rests on fish of 2.5–131 g at 10–30 °C (Hartman et al. 2017; AFS 2011 poster)
claims.location: web page: AFS 2011 abstract P-197 (Porto et al.), Wayback capture of 3 Nov 2016
claims.quote: a variety of sizes of fish (2.5g – 130.7g)
claims.conditions: laboratory measurements of metabolism, growth and consumption at 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 °C; growth and consumption trials one week, individual aquaria, ad libitum; maximum consumption and growth between 20 and 25 °C; built with Fish Bioenergetics 3.0 and 'previously published data'
claims.note: Confirmed in the poster abstract, which is the cited conference item in full. The 2017 article (unread) may have added fish or temperatures; credit the range to the poster (Porto et al. 2011), not to 'Hartman et al. 2017'.

FB4's stored Brown Bullhead row has ED 6700 (Deslauriers_etal_2017.json); whether the article gives it, and for what fish, is unchecked. The project already moved the model's value to 5,000 J/g (src/w3/fish3.js:710-715, 'fatty farmed catfish' → wild ictalurid muscle), so the table and the model may disagree.

claims.claim: the bullhead runs on the FB4 'Brown Bullhead' set (Hartman et al. 2017)
claims.source_value: the set's source is Hartman, K. J. 2017 (single author), TAFS 146(4): 634–644; 'Hartman et al. 2017' is FB4's label
claims.location: FB4 reference list, Deslauriers et al. 2017, p. 595 (PDF p. 10)
claims.quote: Hartman, K. J. 2017. Bioenergetics of Brown Bullhead in a changing climate.
claims.note: Attribution only. The code's values match FB4's row (Deslauriers_etal_2017.json); whether the article prints the same values is unchecked.

claims.claim: below 15 °C the young breathe on the bullhead's own set (Hartman: 41 mg O₂ kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ at 5 g, 4 °C, Q10 2.5)
claims.note: Unchecked against the article. Redone from FB4's row (REQ 1: RA 0.0007, RB −0.271, RQ 0.0915, RTO 0.4055 with a constant swimming speed of 1, so activity × e^0.4055 = 1.50): 0.0007 × 5^−0.271 × e^(0.0915·4) × 1.50 = 0.000979 g O₂ g⁻¹ d⁻¹ = 40.8 mg O₂ kg⁻¹ h⁻¹; Q10 = e^(10 × 0.0915) = 2.50. The arithmetic is right; it is FB4's model, not a measurement at 4 °C (the poster's lowest test temperature was 10 °C).

claims.claim: on FB4's Hartman et al. 2017 set a bullhead needs 0.35–0.56 of its Cmax to hold weight at 18–24 °C (ration falls as W^−0.225, respiration as W^−0.271)
claims.note: The exponents are FB4's CB −0.225 and RB −0.271; the maintenance fractions are the project's arithmetic on FB4's row, not checked here.

notes: The coordinator's lead checks out: Hartman (2017, TAFS 146(4): 634–644) is the peer-reviewed paper behind FB4's bullhead row, and §3.5.4's 'documented only in conference work (no peer-reviewed paper was found)' must go. The rewrite should cite the article for the model (and get a library copy to check the stored values and the fish sizes and temperatures behind them), and the 2011 poster (Porto et al.) only for the 2.5–131 g, 10–30 °C detail if the article is not read. The 2015 talk abstract: PAH-linked tumours in Great Lakes bullheads; warming expected to raise consumption and contaminant exposure; 'Independent laboratory experiments were used to validate model predictions'. The article's abstract: Brown Bullhead is a 'benthic‐oriented warmwater fish'; a 4 °C warming would raise growth in the north of the range and cause declines or extirpation in the south.
